text: Let $R$ be a relation on $\mathrm{ℝ}$, given by $R=\{(a,b):3a-3b+\sqrt{7}$ is an irrational number $\}$. Then $R$ is
options: reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For reflexive :

$3a-3a+\sqrt{7}$ is an irrational number $\forall a\in R,\therefore R$ is reflexive

For symmetric :

Let $3a-3b+\sqrt{7}$ is an irrational number

$\Rightarrow 3b-3a+\sqrt{7}$ is an irrational number

For example, Let $3a-3b=\sqrt{7}$

$\sqrt{7}+\sqrt{7}$ is irrational but $-\sqrt{7}+\sqrt{7}$ is not.

$\therefore R$ is not symmetric

For transitive :

Let $3a-3b+\sqrt{7}$ is irrational and $3b-3c+\sqrt{7}$ is irrational.

$\Rightarrow 3a-3c+\sqrt{7}$ is irrational.

For example, take $a=0,b=-\sqrt{7},c=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}$

$R$ is not transitive.

text:
Let $S$ denote the set of all real values of $λ$ such that the system of equations

$λx+y+z=1$

$x+λy+z=1$

$x+y+λz=1$

is inconsistent, then $\sum\limits _{λ\in S}\left (|λ|^{2}+|λ|\right )$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The coefficient determinant is

$\Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} λ & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & λ & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & λ \end{array}\right |=λ(λ^{2}-1)-(λ-1)+(1-λ)=λ^{3}-3λ+2=(λ-1)^{2}(λ+2).$

For $λ\neq 1,-2$, $\Delta \neq 0$ and the system has a unique solution, so it is consistent.

For $λ=1$, all three equations become $x+y+z=1$, which has infinitely many solutions, so the system is consistent.

For $λ=-2$, adding the three equations gives $(λ+2)(x+y+z)=3$, i.e. $0=3$, which is impossible, so the system is inconsistent.

Thus $S=\{-2\}$ and

$\sum\limits _{λ\in S}\left (|λ|^{2}+|λ|\right )=4+2=6.$

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: Let $S=\left \{x:x\in \mathrm{ℝ}\mathrm{and}(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2})^{x^{2}-4}+(\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2})^{x^{2}-4}=10\right \}$. Then $n(S)$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2})^{x^{2}-4}=t$

$\begin{array}{ll} \quad t+\dfrac{1}{t}=10 \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & t^{2}-10t+1=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & t=\dfrac{10\pm \sqrt{100-4}}{2}=5\pm 2\sqrt{6} \end{array}$

Case-I

$\begin{array}{ll} \quad t=5+2\sqrt{6}=(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2})^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & (\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2})^{x^{2}-4}=(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2})^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & x^{2}-4=2\Rightarrow x^{2}=6\Rightarrow x=\pm \sqrt{6} \end{array}$

Case-II :

$t=5-2\sqrt{6}$ = $(\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2})^{2}$

$(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2})^{x^{2}-4}=(\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2})^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \left ((\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2})^{-1}\right )^{x^{2}-4}=(\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2})^{2}$

$\Rightarrow 4-x^{2}=2$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}=2$

$\Rightarrow x=\pm \sqrt{2}$

text:
The area enclosed by the closed curve $\mathrm{C}$ given by the differential equation 

$\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{x+a}{y-2}=0,y(1)=0$ is $4π$.

Let $P$ and $Q$ be the points of intersection of the curve $\mathrm{C}$ and the $y$-axis. If normals at $P$ and $Q$ on the curve $\mathrm{C}$ intersect $x$-axis at points $R$ and $S$ respectively, then the length of the line segment $RS$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{x+a}{y-2}=0 \\  \\ \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{x+a}{2-y} \\  \\ (2-y)dy=(x+a)dx \\  \\ 2y-\dfrac{y^{2}}{2}=\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}+\mathrm{ax}+\mathrm{c} \\  \\ \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{c}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\text{as}\mathrm{y}(1)=0 \\  \\ \mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{y}^{2}+2\mathrm{ax}-4\mathrm{y}-1-2\mathrm{a}=0 \\  \\ π\mathrm{r}^{2}=4π \\  \\ \mathrm{r}^{2}=4 \\  \\ 2=\sqrt{a^{2}+4+1+2a} \\  \\ (\mathrm{a}+1)^{2}=0 \end{array}$

$P,Q=(0,2\pm \sqrt{3})$

Equation of normal at $\mathrm{P},\mathrm{Q}$ are $\mathrm{y}-2=\sqrt{3}(\mathrm{x}-1)$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{y}-2=-\sqrt{3}(\mathrm{x}-1) \\  \\ \mathrm{R}=\left (1-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}},0\right ) \\  \\ \mathrm{S}=\left (1+\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}},0\right ) \\  \\ \mathrm{RS}=\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3}}=4\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \end{array}$

If $y=y(x)$ is the solution curve of the differential equation 

$\frac{dy}{dx}+y\tan x=x\sec x,0\leq x\leq \frac{π}{3},y(0)=1$, then $y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}+y\tan x=x\sec x$

$\therefore$ I.F $=e^{\int \tan xdx}=\sec x$

$\Rightarrow y\sec x=\int x\sec ^{2}xdx$

$\Rightarrow y\sec x=x\tan x-\ln |\sec x|+c$

Given, $y(0)=1$

$\Rightarrow 1=c$

$\therefore$ $y\sec x=x\tan x-\ln |\sec x|+1$

$\Rightarrow y=x\sin x-\cos x\ln |\sec x|+\cos x$

Now, at $x=π/6$, we have

$\begin{array}{l} y=\dfrac{π}{12}-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\log _{e}\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}+\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  \\ =\dfrac{π}{12}-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\left [\log _{e}\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}-\log _{e}e\right ] \\  \\ =\dfrac{π}{12}-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\log _{e}\left (\dfrac{2}{e\sqrt{3}}\right ) \end{array}$

text: Let $f:\mathrm{ℝ}\to \mathrm{ℝ}$ be a differentiable function such that $f^{'}(x)+f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{2}f(t)dt$. If $f(0)=e^{-2}$, then $2f(0)-f(2)$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f^{'}(x)+f(x)=k$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow e^{x}f(x)=ke^{x}+c \\  \\ f(x)=k+ce^{-x} \\  \\ k=\int\limits _{0}^{2}\left (k+ce^{-t}\right )dt \\  \\ k=2k+c\cdot \dfrac{e^{-t}}{-1}\left |_{0}^{2} \\  \\ k=2k+c\left (\dfrac{e^{-2}}{-1}+1\right ) \\  \\ -k=c\left (1-\dfrac{1}{e^{2}}\right ) \\  \\ f(x)=ce^{-x}-c\left (1-\dfrac{1}{e^{2}}\right ) \\  \\ f(0)=c-c+\dfrac{c}{e^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{e^{2}}\Rightarrow c=1 \\  \\ f(2)=e^{-2}-r\left (1-e^{-2}\right ) \\  \\ =2e^{-2}-1 \\  \\ 2f(0)-f(2)=1 \end{array} \right.$

text: $A(2,6,2),B(-4,0,λ),C(2,3,-1)$ and $D(4,5,0),|λ|\leq 5$ are the vertices of a quadrilateral $ABCD$. If its area is 18 square units, then $5-6λ$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a plane quadrilateral with diagonals $⃗{d}_{1}$ and $⃗{d}_{2}$, the area is $\dfrac{1}{2}|⃗{d}_{1}\times ⃗{d}_{2}|$.

$AC\leftarrow =-3\hat{j}-3\hat{k},BD\leftarrow =8\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-λ\hat{k}$

$AC\leftarrow \times BD\leftarrow =\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 8 & 5 & -λ \end{array}\right |=(3λ+15)\hat{i}-24\hat{j}+24\hat{k}$

Area $=18$ gives $|AC\leftarrow \times BD\leftarrow |=36$:

$(3λ+15)^{2}+24^{2}+24^{2}=36^{2}\Rightarrow (3λ+15)^{2}=144\Rightarrow 3λ+15=\pm 12$

$\Rightarrow λ=-1\text{or}λ=-9$

Since $|λ|\leq 5$, $λ=-1$; for this value the four points are coplanar, as $[AB\leftarrow AC\leftarrow AD\leftarrow ]=0$.

$5-6λ=5+6=11$

Hence, the answer is 11.
